record_under_review.evidence_span: The paper investigates GPU power and thermal fluctuations as side channels for extracting transformer architectural details. It evaluates public language and vision transformers, reports over 89% average model-family identification accuracy and 100% hyperparameter classification in the abstract, and demonstrates transfer attacks with average success above 93%; the paper also describes a user-privilege threat model and responsible disclosure to NVIDIA.
record_under_review.limits: The evidence is an author preprint and the repository does not yet extract every table or repeat the experiments; telemetry access, GPU generation, co-tenancy assumptions, and mitigation effectiveness constrain generalization.
record_under_review.method_or_artifact: CNN-based predictors over power and thermal traces to infer transformer family, layer, and attention-head information, followed by substitute-model construction and black-box transfer attacks.
metrics: over 93% average transfer-attack success in abstract
BERT score above 93 for substitute-model evaluation
record_under_review.problem: Shared or virtualized GPUs expose power and thermal telemetry that may leak proprietary transformer architecture information without physical access.
record_under_review.title: Energon: Unveiling Transformers from GPU Power and Thermal Side-Channels
record_under_review.workload_or_benchmark: Eight publicly available language/vision model families, custom transformers, NVIDIA A40 data-center GPU inference, single-process and noisy multi-process settings.
